text:
B: Hiya! Oh, hang on, are you the Dutch engineer? With the toilet paper trick?
A: Er, yes. Martijn. Walthamstow. Who told you that?
B: Abena! I just had her. She's going home to test her fan tonight. I'm going to do ours an' all. I'm Joanne, by the way, Arnold, Nottingham.
A: Good. Her landlord should fix it. It sounded like the building, not her.
B: Well she won't let him off, I can tell you that. Lovely woman, mind. Gave me some proper good advice about me mum. So what do you build, then?
A: Structures. Residential mostly. At the moment a basement under a Victorian terrace in Islington, which is going badly.
B: Oh no. Why's that?
A: Water in the ground. Neighbours. The architect. In that order, er, possibly reversed.
B: [laughs] Sounds like parents' evening. I'm in a primary school office. I'm the one on the front desk dealing with the dads who've parked on the zigzags.
A: Do you tell them to move?
B: Every single morning, duck. Kindly. And then firmly.
A: Good. Someone has to.
B: What do you do when you're not digging basements?
A: I cycle to work. Parkrun on Saturdays, Lloyd Park, when my daughter isn't staying.
B: Oh, I do parkrun! Colwick Park, every Saturday. What's your time like?
A: Twenty-four, twenty-five minutes. It's gone up a few seconds this year. I keep a spreadsheet.
B: A spreadsheet! [laughs] I'm about thirty-five minutes, and that's me chatting all the way round. I only started after a cancer scare at fifty. It were fine in the end, but it gave me a kick up the backside, you know.
A: That's a good reason. Better than mine. I just like the numbers.
B: Well, whatever gets you out of bed. Then it's coffee after, that's the best bit for me, if I'm honest.
A: I usually go home. Er, maybe I should stay for the coffee.
B: You should! You'd get to know people. That's what it's for really. So you've got a daughter?
A: Fourteen. She's quieter with me now. The girl from Bolton said I should ask her to show me her makeup videos.
B: Oh, that's not bad advice, that. My Becky was exactly the same at fourteen, wouldn't give me the time of day. Now she rings me from Leeds three times a week to moan about her boss.
A: That's reassuring.
B: They come back round. Just keep turning up, do you know what I mean? Even if they're mardy.
A: Mardy?
B: [laughs] Sulky. Grumpy. It's a Nottingham thing.
A: I'll use it. She'll be mardy that I know the word.
